name: Spring PetClinic
summary: PetClinic is a Spring Boot web app for a veterinary clinic: find owners, add pets, record visits, list vets. Each browser request goes through Spring MVC to a controller, which loads or saves data through Spring Data JPA repositories and returns a Thymeleaf page. Data lives in an in-memory H2 database by default, seeded with sample owners, pets and vets at startup.

groups.label: Spring MVC
groups.description: Framework code that routes requests, binds form fields and renders pages. The app configures it; Spring Boot provides it.

groups.label: Controllers
groups.description: One class per area of the app. Each method handles one URL.

groups.label: Data access
groups.description: Spring Data JPA repository interfaces: Spring generates the SQL from method names and annotations.

nodes.label: Browser
nodes.description: Sends page requests and form posts; follows redirects.

nodes.label: Request routing
nodes.description: Spring's DispatcherServlet matches each URL to a controller method. The app adds one interceptor: ?lang=de switches the page language, remembered in the session.

nodes.label: Form binding and validation
nodes.description: Copies form fields onto entities and validates them. PetValidator checks pet name, type and birth date; PetTypeFormatter turns 'cat' into a PetType; @Valid applies the entity's own constraints, like a 10-digit telephone.

nodes.label: Thymeleaf views
nodes.description: HTML templates rendered on the server with the model the controller filled in. A shared layout wraps every page; error.html shows failures.

nodes.label: OwnerController
nodes.description: Find owners by last name (paged, 5 per page), show one owner with their pets and visits, create and edit owners.

nodes.label: PetController
nodes.description: Add and edit an owner's pets. Rejects duplicate names for the same owner and birth dates in the future.

nodes.label: VisitController
nodes.description: Book a visit for a pet. The visit date must be in the future.

nodes.label: VetController
nodes.description: Lists vets as an HTML page (/vets.html, paged) or as JSON (/vets).

nodes.label: Welcome and error demo
nodes.description: The home page, and /oups, which throws on purpose to show the error page.

nodes.label: OwnerRepository
nodes.description: Loads owners by id or by last-name prefix (paged) and saves them. Saving an owner also saves its new pets and visits (cascade).

nodes.label: PetTypeRepository
nodes.description: Lists the pet types (cat, dog, lizard...) for the pet form's dropdown.

nodes.label: VetRepository
nodes.description: Lists vets with their specialties. Both findAll methods are cached in the 'vets' cache.

nodes.label: Vets cache
nodes.description: A JCache cache named 'vets' (Caffeine), created in CacheConfiguration. Repeated vet lookups skip the database.

nodes.label: Database
nodes.description: H2 in memory by default. Run with the mysql or postgres profile to use those instead; connection settings are in the matching properties file.

nodes.label: Schema and sample data
nodes.description: SQL scripts run at startup for the chosen database: tables, a unique (owner, pet name) constraint, and sample owners, pets and vets.

nodes.label: Owners, pets, visits
nodes.description: Owner has many Pets (loaded eagerly, ordered by name); Pet has a PetType and many Visits.

nodes.label: Vets and specialties
nodes.description: Vet has many Specialties. Vets wraps the list for the JSON endpoint.

nodes.label: Base entities
nodes.description: Shared superclasses: BaseEntity (id), NamedEntity (name), Person (first and last name).

steps.text: The user searches for a last name: GET /owners?lastName=Davis.
Spring routes it to OwnerController.processFindForm.
The controller asks for page 1 of owners whose last name starts with Davis, 5 per page.
findByLastNameStartingWith becomes a LIKE query.
Two owners match.
Several matches, so it shows the list. One match would redirect straight to that owner; none shows the form with 'not found'.
ownersList.html renders the table.
The user submits the new-pet form for owner 1.
Before the handler runs, @ModelAttribute methods load the owner and the pet types.
Form fields are copied onto a new Pet and PetValidator checks it.
It also rejects a name this owner already uses and a birth date in the future.
The pet is added to the owner and the owner is saved; the new pet is inserted by cascade.
INSERT INTO pets. The unique (owner, name) constraint is a second guard against duplicates.
The browser is redirected to the owner's page, which shows the new pet.
GET /vets asks for the vet list as JSON.
The controller wraps the list in a Vets object and returns it as the response body.
findAll is @Cacheable("vets").
The first call misses and runs the query; later calls are served from the cache.
On a miss: vets and their specialties are loaded.
PetClinicApplication starts Spring Boot, which configures Spring MVC, JPA and Thymeleaf.
Spring Boot runs db/h2/schema.sql and data.sql (or the mysql or postgres versions).
The database now has 10 owners, 13 pets and 6 vets.
CacheConfiguration creates the empty 'vets' cache.

steps.text: showResourcesVetList() asks the repository for all vets. Because of @ResponseBody, the result becomes JSON, not a template.
findAll() is annotated @Cacheable("vets"), so Spring checks the cache before running the query.
First request since startup: the vets cache is empty, so the query runs.
The vets cache already holds the list. It is returned immediately; the database is not touched.
Load the vets and their specialties.

select s.* from vet_specialties vs
  join specialties s on s.id = vs.specialty_id
 where vs.vet_id in (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6)

steps.text: The result is stored in the vets cache for the next request.
The Vets object is written as JSON by Spring's message converter.
The script gets the vet list as JSON.
